text:
mira: Quick bench ask — can someone run an onboarding smoke + perf pass for model `tundra-6.5b` (fp16 and int8) on p4d-prod? Need per-token latencies, p95/p99, and peak GPU memory. Target context=2048; please test batch=1,4,8. Prefer strip-down eval (generate 256 tokens) so we can get numbers quickly. Ideally results by EOD. Thanks! :pray:
sam: I can grab it. Kicking off smoke on one p4d now. Which config should I compare against as a baseline?
mira: Use `prod-stable-7b` numbers as baseline (we've been using that for context). If possible include a short note on generation quality regressions (sampling sanity) — just a quick check, not full eval.
bench-bot: Running smoke bench: model=tundra-6.5b, node=p4d-prod-12, ctx=2048, gen=256, wandb=off. Will publish raw outputs when done.
bench-bot: DONE — summary below:
```
model: tundra-6.5b (fp16)
platform: p4d-prod-12
config: ctx=2048, gen=256
batch=1  mean_token_latency=3.8ms  p95=9.6ms  p99=18.2ms  throughput=263 tok/s  gpu_mem_peak=16.2GB
batch=4  mean_token_latency=5.1ms  p95=12.4ms p99=26.7ms  throughput=940 tok/s  gpu_mem_peak=20.1GB
batch=8  mean_token_latency=7.9ms  p95=21.8ms p99=45.3ms  throughput=1760 tok/s gpu_mem_peak=24.5GB
notes: small jitter on p99 for batch>=4, likely due to K/V eviction in long ctx.
```
bench-bot: Additional run (int8 quant @4bit-like) on same node:
```
model: tundra-6.5b (int8-quant)
batch=1 mean_token_latency=4.5ms p95=11.2ms p99=22.9ms throughput=222 tok/s gpu_mem_peak=9.8GB
batch=4 mean_token_latency=6.0ms p95=14.8ms p99=31.2ms throughput=805 tok/s gpu_mem_peak=13.4GB
```
evan: Thanks for the publish. Quick read: fp16 batch=1 mean 3.8ms is decent, baseline prod-stable-7b was ~3.2ms in our last scan — so ~18% slower per token but much cheaper memory footprint than larger models. The int8 memory wins look promising.
sam: Observed one error in the logs during the fp16 batch=8 run — a transient CUDA alloc warning just before a p99 spike. Pasted from node logs:
```
[2025-04-07T14:02:33Z] WARN cuda_alloc: fallback_alloc failed, trying GC
[2025-04-07T14:02:33Z] INFO kv_cache: evicting 128MB prefix chunks
```
sam: I think K/V eviction + GC could explain p99 spikes for long ctx. Will rerun with smaller max_kv_memory and collector tuning.
liz: For next steps: (1) sam to rerun targeted tail-latency scan with GC tuning (2) evan to run 30s steady-state rps test at 50 and 200 concurrency to see service behavior under load (3) mira to add quick sampling QA for 10 prompts and confirm no obvious hallucination/regression.
mira: Sounds good. Sam — can you also dump `nv-top` snapshot around the p99 spike so we have thread stacks? That helps perf team triage.
sam: Yup. I'll run the rerun and attach nvprof snapshot. Expect publish in ~2 hours.
evan: One more ask — can bench-bot include a tiny perf histogram for per-token latencies (json) in the publish? Even coarse buckets help.
bench-bot: Acked — adding histogram to the rerun artifact.
mira: Thanks all — appreciate the quick turnaround. If rerun confirms p99 root cause is KV GC, we can try a short canary on Dedicated with slightly larger KV caps before wider rollout. :rocket:
liz: Marking action items in the onboard checklist. I'll follow up in the canary channel once sam posts the rerun.
sam: Rerun queued (priority=high). Will post results + logs to this thread.
mira: :thumbsup:
